posts.pinComment: Shadow workflows + agents: Comment OPS for the seven-question ops checklist (approvals + publish planes + STOP).
posts.text:
Shadow workflows are not speed. They are risk transferred to your future self.

If your AI flow lives in side chats, private tabs, and undocumented handoffs, you do not have an ops system yet.

You have a luck system.

Fix the path, not the person: approved route, clear owner, visible audit trail.

Founders/operators scaling agent workflows: DM me "OPS" and I will send the practical checklist.
Hiring for AI implementation + delivery ownership? I am open to the right role.

Daily AI pro tip:
Give every automation path one approved execution route and one named owner, or shadow tooling will quietly become your real production system.

posts.pinComment: Prod truth + agents: Comment OPS for the checklist link.
posts.text:
"We tested in staging" only helps when staging is real.

If production is the first place your workflow meets real load, real users, and real edge cases, production is your test plan.

Design for truth: monitors, rollback criteria, and explicit human gate points.

Teams shipping AI features and tired of demo-only confidence: DM me "OPS" for the production-readiness checklist.

Daily AI pro tip:
Run one canary generation against production inputs before a bigger batch so auth, schema, and provider failures show up early instead of publicly.

posts.pinComment: Knowledge + agents: Comment OPS for the doc.
posts.text:
Documentation is not a file. It is ownership.

When nobody owns updates, retrieval becomes a rumor amplifier.

The boring controls win: owner, review cadence, expiry, archive rule.

That is how knowledge becomes infrastructure.

If your team is scaling agents and your docs are drifting, DM me "OPS".

Daily AI pro tip:
Attach freshness dates and explicit owners to retrieval sources so accurate models do not become confidently outdated assistants.

posts.pinComment: Buyer / vendor reality: Comment OPS for the checklist.
posts.text:
If the vendor deck says "AI" ten times and "failure mode" zero times, you are buying a mood, not a system.

Serious buying questions: evaluation harness, rollback behavior, human override, and export path.

Real operators welcome hard questions.

If you are evaluating agent vendors this quarter, DM me "OPS" for my due-diligence prompts.

Daily AI pro tip:
The cheapest vendor demo is often the most expensive integration, so score tools on fallback behavior and exportability before you score them on polish.

posts.pinComment: Incidents + automation: Comment OPS for gates + STOP.
posts.text:
Automation at 2 a.m. still needs ownership at 2 a.m.

"The bot handles it" is not incident design.

Define the contract: what auto-remediates, what must page a human, what is never allowed to auto-fire.

This is where trust is built.

Need to harden your on-call + AI workflow? DM me "OPS".

Daily AI pro tip:
Tag every failed run with an incident owner and request id automatically so triage starts with context instead of a search party.
